Article Title: Congress cites Maniben’s diary, seeks apology from Rajnath
Article Text:
Union minister for defence Rajnath Singh (PTI photo)

After Rajnath's Babri Remark, Sonia Targets BJP In Fiery Counterattack Over Maligning Nehru Legacy

NEW DELHI: Sharing excerpts from a book containing Vallabhbhai Patel ’s daught-er’s diaries, Congress Saturday accused defence minister Rajnath Singh of lying that Jawaharlal Nehru wanted to build the Babri mosque using public funds, and demanded that Singh apologise to the nation for spreading falsehoods about the country’s first PM.Two days after Singh’s remarks made headlines, Congress spokesman Jairam Ramesh said the minister is sp-reading falsehoods about Nehru to “improve his relationship” with PM Narendra Modi. Ramesh posted on X Maniben’s original diary entry in Gujarati on pages 212-213 in the book ‘Samarpit Padchhayo Sardarno’ by CA RS Patel ‘Aaresh’, that was published by the Sardar Patel Vallabhbhai Patel Memorial Society, 2025.“There is a huge differe-nce between what is contai-ned in the original diary entry and what Rajnath Singh and his fellow ‘distorians’ a-re propagating,” the spokesman said, adding, “The defe-nce minister must apologise for the falsehoods he is spre-ading, simply to improve his relationship with the PM.”A row broke out after Singh made the claim at a rally in Gujarat, with Congress calling his remarks a “lie” and “WhatsApp university story”. BJP had cited Maniben as the source of the claim.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh claimed Jawaharlal Nehru wanted to build the Babri mosque using public funds. Congress spokesman Jairam Ramesh said the minister is sp-reading falsehoods about Nehru to “improve his relationship” with PM Narendra Modi.

Article Title: Signs of truce as Shinde, Maharas BJP chief share stage
Article Text:
Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis with his deputy Eknath Shinde (File photo)

'Maligning Hindu Way Of Life': PM Modi Calls Out Colonial Mindset Over 'Hindu Rate Of Growth' Label

THANE: After weeks of escalating tensions between BJP and Shiv Sena in the Kalyan LS constituency over poaching of each other’s activists, Maharashtra BJP chief Ravindra Chavan shared stage with Dy CM Eknath Shinde and Kalyan MP Shrikant Shinde at the bhoomipujan of a Rs 180-crore multi-purpose sports complex, war memorial and several other projects in Dombivli.Their coming together signalled a possible pause in the ongoing conflict ahead of local body polls, where Sena has accused Chavan of poaching its workers. Chavan had also said accusations during elections were natural but stressed that BJP, Shiv Sena, and NCP had been functioning well together for the past year. — Pradeep Gupta
Article Summary: Ravindra Chavan and Eknath Shinde shared stage at the bhoomipujan of a Rs 180-crore multi-purpose sports complex, war memorial and several other projects in Dombivli. Their coming together signalled a possible pause in the ongoing conflict ahead of local body polls.

Article Title: IYC moves HC against decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as protest site
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Indian Youth Congress (IYC) Wednesday moved Delhi High Court challenging Delhi Police ’s decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a designated site for protests and demonstrations.The application was filed in a pending petition by IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib, who had earlier approached the court seeking permission to hold protests at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.In its latest plea, IYC challenged Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar’s standing order dated Oct 11, under which Jantar Mantar was denotified and Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi were designated as alternative venues for protests and demonstrations.
Article Summary: Indian Youth Congress (IYC) Wednesday moved Delhi High Court challenging Delhi Police’s decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a designated site for protests and demonstrations. The application was filed in a pending petition by IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib.

Article Title: Dhami government took steps at every level in Ankita Bhandari case: U'khand BJP chief
Article Text:
Dhami government took steps at every level in Ankita Bhandari case: U'khand BJP chief

Uttarakhand BJP chief Mahendra Bhatt on Wednesday said the state took steps at every stage in the Ankita Bhandari case and ensured an impartial investigation.Bhatt said the Pushkar Dhami government treated the murder case with seriousness and ensured the accused were arrested right after the crime was unravelled.He said the government also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) and made arrangements for prosecution and addressing the family's demands.The remarks of the Rajya Sabha MP came against the backdrop of a protest at India Gate in the national capital by Bhandari's parents, who were joined in their demand for justice by Rahul Gandhi, the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition.Bhandari, an employee at a resort in Uttarakhand, was murdered in September 2022.Bhatt dismissed the Congress's allegation that the probe into the receptionist's killing was laced with malice."Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami made it clear from the outset that the safety of women and strict action against criminals are the government's top priorities. Accordingly, instructions were issued to the police for immediate action. The accused were arrested and sent to jail within 24 hours of the incident coming to light," he said.A chargesheet was submitted to the court based on evidence and witness testimonies, and the "prosecution effectively argued the case in court," he said."Through the judicial process, the guilty were sentenced to life imprisonment; this verdict was delivered based on the evidence presented and established legal procedures," Bhatt said.The BJP leader said the Dhami government also acceded to Bhandari's parents' demand for a CBI probe, and that they were given Rs 25 lakh in financial support."The issue of securing justice for Ankita Bhandari extends beyond a mere criminal case; it is also linked to women's safety, sensitive governance, and public trust in the legal system," he added. PTI
Article Summary: Uttarakhand BJP chief Mahendra Bhatt said the state took steps at every stage in the Ankita Bhandari case and ensured an impartial investigation. He said the Pushkar Dhami government treated the murder case with seriousness and ensured the accused were arrested. Bhatt dismissed the Congress's allegation that the probe into the receptionist's killing was laced with malice.

Article Title: 'Consistently sides with those who exploit women': BJP targets Congress over Akoijam's dismissal from JNU
Article Text:
Prof Angomcha Bimol Akoijam.

NEW DELHI: BJP on Thursday attacked Congress over dismissal of its Inner Manipur MP, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment allegations by female students.Addressing reporters, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accused the Congress leadership of remaining silent on the issue and alleged that the party was siding with those accused of exploiting women.“It is highly unfortunate that the Congress party consistently sides with those who exploit women. When Bimal Akoijam, a sitting MP from the Congress party, sexually harassed 11 female students, JNU’s internal committee found that the complaints filed by these students against him were truthful and substantiated by facts. Consequently, on October 9, 2026, Bimal Akoijam was dismissed from his position at JNU,” the BJP MP said.“Yet, there is an absolutely deafening silence from Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Kharge ji, and Sonia Gandhi... Today, under the guidance and leadership of our Mahila Morcha National President and fellow MP, Rupkumari Choudhary, we met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Om Birla.... We appealed to the President, Droupadi Murmu.Yesterday, a delegation met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW), Vijaya Rahatkar, and today, we submitted a memorandum to Om Birla. We had a very productive discussion...” she added.Earlier on Wednesday, Delhi Police has served a notice to Akoijam, asking him to join an investigation into the allegations. The notice comes days after police registered an FIR following a complaint forwarded by JNU’s chief security officer for necessary legal action, news agency PTI reported.The documents submitted to the police included the university’s dismissal order, the internal committee’s inquiry report and its assessment of the allegations.The FIR invokes provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to sexual harassment and words, gestures or acts intended to insult a woman’s modesty. Police documents refer to an incident on May 6 and an unspecified period before that date.Akoijam, a professor at JNU’s Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences, was dismissed with immediate effect on October 9 following an internal inquiry.According to reports, several female students filed sexual harassment complaints against Akoijam in May. The allegations included claims that he invited students to his campus residence under the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to sexually harass them. Some students also alleged that he made inappropriate remarks in class.Akoijam has denied the allegations, describing the complaints as politically motivated. He has also challenged the university’s account of the inquiry process.
Article Summary: BJP attacks Congress over dismissal of its Inner Manipur MP, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment allegations by female students. Delhi Police has served a notice to A Koijam, asking him to join an investigation into the allegations.

Article Title: 'They silence voices of victims': Rahul, Kharge slam detention of Ankita Bhandari's parents
Article Text:
Rahul, Kharge slam detention of Ankita Bhandari’s parents

NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday criticised the detention of Ankita Bhandari’s parents, alleging they were taken into custody while peacefully protesting against Dushyant Gautam’s proposed appointment as Sikkim Governor.Rahul said the Congress would stand by the family until they received justice, asserting that their fight would neither be silenced nor stopped.“4 AM in the morning. While the world was asleep, Ankita Bhandari's parents were taken into custody. Their crime? They were sitting quietly at India Gate—with heavy shoulders, without any commotion, and simply demanding that Dushyant Gautam should not be made the Governor of Sikkim until the CBI investigation is complete," Rahul said in a post on X."Yesterday, Priyanka and I met these parents. Even before the results of that investigation came in, the appointment was rushed, and the parents asking questions were picked up in the dead of night. This is the hallmark of this government: silence the voices of the victims, remove those who ask questions. But the fight for justice will neither be silenced nor stopped. The Congress stands with Ankita Bhandari's family, and will continue to stand—until they get justice," he added.Earlier in the day, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge described the action as the "pinnacle of the Modi government's cowardice and insensitivity."Kharge criticised the Centre, saying the parents seeking justice had been detained while a BJP "VIP" was rewarded with a gubernatorial post."The pinnacle of the Modi government's cowardice and insensitivity! The parents of Ankita Bhandari, who are pleading for justice, are taken into custody, while a BJP 'VIP' is rewarded with the Governor's post! This oppression by those in power is not a sign of the government's strength, but rather proof of its attempt to flee from questions," Kharge said in a post on X."Such treatment of parents who have already lost their daughter is utterly shameful and reprehensible. The Congress Party will continue to fight to ensure justice for daughter Ankita," he added.Ankita Bhandari’s parents, who were detained by Delhi Police during an overnight protest at India Gate in the early hours of Thursday, were released from Tilak Marg Police Station around 5 am on October 15.The family, along with several opposition leaders and protesters, was demanding that the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim Governor be put on hold until the ongoing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Ankita’s murder is completed. They have cited alleged links and sought a halt to his appointment pending the investigation.Speaking to reporters, Ankita’s father, Virendra Singh Bhandari, said, "If Dushyant Kumar's appointment is not canceled within 24 hours, we will stage nationwide protests once again. The government will be held accountable for this."Congress leaders Pawan Khera, Supriya Shrinate and Qazi Nizamuddin criticised the police action, alleging that authorities were targeting those demanding justice for Ankita and questioning Gautam’s appointment.Ankita was murdered on September 18, 2022, and her body was recovered from the Chilla Canal on September 24, 2022.
Article Summary: Ankita Bhandari’s parents were detained by Delhi Police during an overnight protest at India Gate in the early hours of Thursday. The family, along with several opposition leaders and protesters, was demanding that the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim Governor be put on hold until the ongoing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe is completed.

NEW DELHI: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee is facing two separate legal proceedings in Delhi. A fresh defamation suit has been filed against him at the Saket court over a video allegedly claiming that Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile.Separately, Rathee has been served fresh summons in a 2018 criminal defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey over a video titled "BJP IT Cell Part 2".Supreme Court Advocate-on-Record Amita Sachdeva and other petitioners had approached the Delhi high court over the video titled “Can Hindus Eat BEEF? and prayed before the court to issue directions granting an interim restraint on Rathee from creating, uploading, or publishing similar content."Some time ago, Dhruv Rathee published a video claiming that Lord Shri Ram and Mother Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile. We took the matter regarding that video to the Delhi High Court, and the Delhi High Court directed the Govt of India to have the video removed.""On July 15, 2026, the Govt of India directed YouTube to take down the video, after which that petition was disposed of. Following the disposal of the petition, someone extracted a three-minute segment from that 21-minute video and re-uploaded it,” she added.According to Sachdeva, the petitioners approached the Delhi High Court again, which granted them liberty to initiate fresh legal proceedings against Rathee."We approached the Delhi High Court again. The Court granted us the liberty to file a fresh petition or suit against Dhruv Rathee and seek appropriate relief. Acting on that liberty, we filed a suit today in the Saket Court, before the Learned District Judge, seeking a declaration, an injunction, and damages for defamation; the matter was listed for hearing today," she said.Sachdeva said the petitioner's senior counsel, Makarand Natkar, appeared through video conferencing but could not complete his submissions because of technical difficulties. The court subsequently adjourned the matter to November 5."Today, my senior counsel, Makarand Natkar, presented his submissions. He appeared via video conferencing (VC), but due to some technical issues with the VC connection, the submissions could not be completed. Consequently, the Learned District Judge adjourned the matter to November 5, when we will present our fresh submissions," she added.The complainants, who identified themselves as Hindu devotees, alleged that the video hurt their religious sentiments. The suit also seeks an ex-parte ad-interim injunction restraining Google from restoring, hosting, uploading, sharing or disseminating the video, or any video identical or similar in content, after notice and verification of the URL, during the pendency of the suit.Separately, a Delhi court has issued fresh summons to Rathee in a defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey in 2018. The court noted that attempts to serve Rathee had continued for several years.Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain was hearing Pandey's plea seeking fresh summons. In an order dated October 12, the court said, "From the available record, it is clear that the complainant has been trying to serve the accused no. 1 (Rathee) since the last several years..."Appearing for Pandey, advocate Samaksh Sharma submitted that Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria and had come to India for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. He argued that fresh summons were necessary to ensure prompt steps could be taken to serve the accused.The court permitted fresh summons to be served through dasti service, allowing the complainant to accompany the process server. Rathee has since been physically served at his Gurugram residence. The proceedings had remained pending amid unsuccessful attempts to serve him since 2019.Speaking about the notice served on Rathee, Pandey said, "The court summons has been pasted outside Dhruv Rathee's home because he was not coming out. This stems from eight years ago when Dhruv Rathee created around three videos alleging that I offered Rs 50 lakh to someone to spread fake news against him.”“When Arvind Kejriwal amplified this fake news by tweeting and retweeting it, I filed a case against both Kejriwal and Dhruv Rathee. While Arvind Kejriwal offered an apology, Dhruv Rathee never appeared before the court. Consequently, a notice and summons were issued, which my lawyer pasted outside his Gurugram home..." he added.The case also reached the Supreme Court in connection with a retweet of the video by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal. In February 2024, Kejriwal told the apex court that he had made a mistake by retweeting it.The cases come days after Delhi and Gurugram Police detained Rathee at his Sector 56 residence in Gurugram on October 10, ahead of his planned participation in a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. He was released after around 22 hours.The detention took place amid protests in Delhi led by the CJP, which has been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests saw extensive security arrangements, barricading, traffic restrictions and the detention of protesters.
Article Summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee is facing two separate legal proceedings in Delhi. A fresh defamation suit has been filed against him at the Saket court over a video allegedly claiming that Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile. Separately, Rathee has been served fresh summons in a 2018 criminal defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey.

Article Title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi , Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justice Joymalya Bagchi, said issuing notice on the petition did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.“We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing,” the CJI said, referring to Rahul.During the hearing, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “We are not sitting in ivory towers, we are aware of statements made outside the Court” after lawyers referred to attempts to “browbeat” the judiciary through the march. The CJI said the court would ask Rahul to explain how crowds entered the Supreme Court premises during the demonstration.The INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli – March for Democracy’, led by Rahul, brought thousands of supporters into central Delhi on October 12. The opposition was demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise over alleged electoral irregularities.The march saw supporters gather along roads between Connaught Place and the Supreme Court, waving party flags and raising slogans.Police stopped the procession near Barakhamba Road, where some demonstrators pushed through barricades as security personnel attempted to hold them back. The crowd later gathered along Bhagwan Das Road, with some supporters climbing onto parked police vehicles and buses.Rahul was joined by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav and other INDIA bloc leaders. The procession followed the CJI’s refusal to meet opposition representatives seeking to submit a memorandum on alleged electoral irregularities. He had advised them to file a formal petition, citing matters already pending before the court.The opposition’s separate petition challenging the SIR process alleges arbitrary voter deletions and seeks greater transparency and safeguards in the revision of electoral rolls. The Supreme Court also issued notice to the Election Commission of India on that plea.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notices to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court. The bench, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, said issuing notice on the petition did not mean it was condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.

Article Title: ‘Stop protecting the VIP’: Ankita Bhandari's parents detained after overnight protest over governor appointment
Article Text:
Congress backs parents as Delhi Police break up overnight dharna

After an overnight vigil at India Gate, a pre-dawn swoop by Delhi Police brought the dharna for “Justice to Ankita Bhandari” to an end. The cops arrived at the protest site at 4 am and took away the wailing parents of Ankita Bhandari, who was murdered in Uttarakhand in 2022.Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and, later, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening to express solidarity with the parents. After they left, scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna. Uttarakhand MLA and Congress office-bearer Qazi Nizamuddin, MPs Pawan Khera, Jothi Mani and Imran Pratapgarhi, Congress spokespersons Supriya Shrinate, Gurdeep Sappal and Ragini Nayak, Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib, NSUI president Vinod Jakhar and Mahila Congress president Alka Lamba, among others, joined the vigil, which continued until early morning before being disrupted by the cops.Videos of the police action went viral, with Chib, Jakhar and others even trying to intercept the bus carrying the detainees.Ankita’s parents arrived from Uttarakhand on Wednesday evening and sat on a dharna along with activist Yogita Bhayana, holding a placard that read, “Stop protecting the VIP”. The continuing controversy over Ankita’s murder received a fresh lease of life with the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Gautam as governor.The controversy revolves around the “VIP” who had allegedly sought “special service” at the infamous resort then owned by the son of a BJP leader. Ankita resisted the pressure. Her body was found in a canal in 2022, leading to a murder case.In a social media post, the Congress said there were allegations that Gautam was the “VIP” in question. “Narendra Modi has rewarded Gautam with the governorship of Sikkim. The girls and women of the country are watching how Modi and his govt are protecting Gautam.Instead of giving them justice, the entire BJP govt is hellbent on suppressing the voice of Ankita’s parents,” it said.Ankita’s father urged the President of India to put Gautam’s appointment as governor on hold until the CBI inquiry into the issue is completed.Ankita’s parents were taken by the cops to Tilak Marg police station, where they were swiftly joined by Congress leaders protesting the police action against the parents, who were seeking justice for their deceased daughter.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AICC general secretary KC Venugopal visited the protest site on Wednesday evening. Scores of Congress MPs, MLAs and workers of the Youth Congress and NSUI, among others, joined the dharna.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Probationary sub-inspector booked for harassing wife, threatening her with service pistol
Article Text:
Pune:





Sahakarnagar police have registered a domestic violence case against a probationary police sub-inspector after his wife alleged that he harassed her for money and threatened her with his service pistol.The complainant (31) alleged that her husband (29), who is posted at Sahakarnagar police station, harassed her for money to buy a car and a flat in Pune.“The sub-inspector and the complainant got married in 2022. It was a love marriage. The couple hails from Beed,” senior inspector Vitthal Pawar of Sahakarnagar police station told TOI.“They fell in love when he was preparing for the civil services examination. He was selected as a sub-inspector and posted in Pune city, following which he and his wife moved here. During their stay in Pune, his wife alleged that he started harassing her, demanding money to buy a car and a flat,” Pawar said.“When his wife confronted him, he allegedly threatened her with his service pistol,” he added.
Article Summary: Police have registered a domestic violence case against a probationary police sub-inspector. His wife alleged that he harassed her for money and threatened her with his service pistol. The couple fell in love when he was preparing for the civil services examination.

Article Title: Gadkari stresses on high voter turnout for Grads’ election
Article Text:
Gadkari MLC polls meet





Nagpur: Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Wednesday asked teachers and professors to ensure their votes were not rendered invalid and to take colleagues along to vote in Nagpur Graduates’ Constituency election.Gadkari was addressing a meet of teachers, professors and educationists organised by the Manthan group at Gadkari Wada in Mahal to campaign for BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale.Spelling out what he expected from those present, he said, “Power, struggle and beauty never last forever. Everyone must therefore recognise their responsibility and work with strength and cooperation for Kohale’s campaign.”Pointing out that the party had won the constituency several times earlier, Gadkari said, “Every voter must recognise the value of the vote and work to raise the polling percentage.”Convener Vishnu Changde briefed the gathering on the Manthan group’s work and earlier programmes. Gadkari answered questions from teachers and professors on their issues.Separately, Kohale addressed graduates’ meets in BJP’s Trimurti Nagar and Subhash Nagar mandals in the city.Kohale explained to the voters what set this contest apart. “The graduates’ constituency election is for educated voters and its nature is different from a general election.Personal relations with voters, consistent contact by workers and the ability to reach every voter are crucial in this election,” he said.He asked workers, who had made door-to-door visits to register graduate voters, to explain the importance of voting and ensure voters turn up on polling day.Kohale pointed out that the seat was associated with CM Devendra Fadnavis and Gadkari. “We have got an opportunity this time to erase the regret of having lost this seat earlier,” he said while urging all workers to campaign unitedly.BJP Nagpur city president Dayashankar Tiwari and city election in-charge Girish Deshmukh attended both mandal meets.
Article Summary: Gadkari was addressing a meet of teachers, professors and educationists at Gadkari Wada in Mahal to campaign for BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale. Kohale addressed graduates’ meets in BJP’s Trimurti Nagar and Subhash Nagar mandals.

Article Title: HC upholds acceptance of 6 AIADMK MLAs resignation
Article Text:
Chennai:





In a reprieve to the ruling TVK govt in Tamil Nadu, the Madras high court on Friday dismissed pleas moved by AIADMK whip Agri S Krishnamurthy and others challenging the Assembly speaker’s decision to accept the resignations of six AIADMK MLAs.The six MLAs cross-voted in favour of the TVK govt during a confidence motion and later joined the ruling TVK.The first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan held that the resignation tendered by the defecting MLAs was ‘genuine and voluntary‘ and in terms of provision enshrined under the X Schedule of the Constitution.“The speaker of Tamil Nadu legislative assembly was not required to undertake a roving or fishing inquiry into the alleged motives behind them. Apparently, their acceptance and the consequential declaration of vacancies are constitutionally valid,” the court said.The pendency of disqualification proceedings did not constitutionally bar the speaker from accepting the resignations, as resignation and disqualification are two distinct constitutional processes. The speaker was therefore competent to accept the resignation notwithstanding the pending disqualification proceedings, the judges added.“The acceptance of resignations does not render the pending disqualification proceedings academic or infructuous. The speaker shall still finally adjudicate and decide the disqualification proceedings, and such determination shall carry the consequences prescribed under the X Schedule of the Constitution,” the bench said.The court asserted that the high court possesses the power under Article 226 of the Constitution to intervene where the speaker fails to decide disqualification proceedings within a reasonable period. “In the peculiar circumstances, a time-bound mandamus is being issued directing the speaker to conclude the disqualification proceedings finally within two months,” the court said.The primary contention of the petitioners was that the speaker should not have accepted the resignations of the MLAs before deciding the disqualification proceedings for crossvoting in favour of the TVK govt violating party whip.Addressing the issue as to whether the speaker was obligated to conduct a proper detailed inquiry before accepting the resignations of the defecting MLAs, the court said, “Under the sky, there is no room for speculations or presumptions for expecting the court or the speaker to inquire into the reasons behind the resignation or conduct any roving enquiry in relation thereof. The enquiry is only for the limited purpose of ascertaining whether the resignation is genuinely prepared and being tendered by the person concerned himself or through his authorised representative and whether it is not under duress, compulsion or undue influence. ”Beyond this limited enquiry, the speaker cannot be required to stand in the shoes of an enquiry officer and undertake a detailed fishing enquiry, the bench added.
Article Summary: The six MLAs cross-voted in favour of the TVK govt during a confidence motion and later joined the ruling TVK. Madras high court dismissed pleas moved by AIADMK whip Agri S Krishnamurthy and others challenging the Assembly speaker’s decision.

Article Title: Two guest workers arrested for recording woman bathing
Article Text:
Device kept inside box

Chennai:





Two workers were arrested on Monday for keeping a mobile phone in a staff bathroom at a house in Anna Nagar East to record a woman bathing. Police seized two mobile phones and found that the accused had also created a fake social media account in the woman’s name.The incident came to light on Oct 12 when the woman, employed as a child caretaker, noticed a box with a hole in it, in the wash room for domestic staff. On checking the box, she found a mobile phone recording her. She handed the device to the homeowner, Lalithkumar, who lodged a complaint at Anna Nagar police station.Police identified the accused as Sanjukumar Thandi, 21, and Ashok Kumar Yadav , 33, both from Bihar , and workers at the house. Investigators found that they had placed the phone inside the box to record the woman without her knowledge and had been accessing a fake social media account in her name.Police registered a case and arrested the two men. They were produced before a magistrate’s court and remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The incident came to light on Oct 12 when the woman, employed as a child caretaker, noticed a box with a hole in it, in the wash room for domestic staff. On checking the box, she found a mobile phone recording her. She handed the device to the homeowner, who lodged a complaint at Anna Nagar police station.

Article Title: Former VAO sentenced to four years in jail for taking bribe of ₹1,000
Article Text:
Krishnagiri

:





A former village administrative officer (VAO) of Thuppuganapalli village in Hosur taluk was sentenced to four years’ rigorous imprisonment in a 2015 bribery case by the principal district court, in Krishnagiri, on Tuesday. The court also imposed a fine of ₹4,000 on him.According to court sources, a village resident had applied to transfer a patta from his mother’s name to his and his father’s names. “M Rajini, who was then village administrative officer, allegedly demanded ₹1,000 to process the application,” said a court official.The complainant approached the directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) in Krishnagiri, which laid a trap. Officials caught Rajini red-handed while accepting ₹1,000 from the complainant. He was arrested and remanded in judicial custody.Following investigation, DVAC filed a chargesheet against Rajini. Principal district judge VR Latha found him guilty and imposed the prison term and fine.
Article Summary: A former village administrative officer (VAO) of Thuppuganapalli village in Hosur taluk was sentenced to four years’ rigorous imprisonment in a 2015 bribery case by the principal district court, in Krishnagiri, on Tuesday. The court also imposed a fine of ₹4,000 on him. A village resident had applied to transfer a patta from his mother’s name to his and his father's names.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Kadayanallur DMK MLA, five others booked in land grabbing case
Article Text:
Kadayanallur DMK MLA, five others booked in land grabbing case

Tenkasi:





The Tenkasi district crime branch unit has registered a case against Kadayanallur DMK MLA T M Rajendran and five others for grabbing a land belonging to a differently abled person using forged documents.The FIR was registered on Oct 9 against Rajendran, his brother Chelladurai, VAO Arulmari, zonal deputy tahsildar Mohideen Pattani, land survey firka officer of Kurukkalpatti Usha and the sub-registrar of Melaneelithanallur. The case pertains to registrations allegedly made between 2008 and 2019.According to the FIR, complainant Murugaiah, a differently abled resident of Akkamalai in Coimbatore district, alleged that his family's ancestral land measuring about 9.7 acres in Thirumalapuram village was illegally transferred through fraudulent documentation.Murugaiah alleged that land standing in the joint names of his late father and uncle was sold and subsequently registered through a series of transactions without obtaining legal heir certificates or the consent of rightful heirs. He further claimed that the land was later converted into housing plots and sold to third parties.The complainant also alleged that portions of the land were encroached upon and included in property declarations submitted by the MLA during the 2026 assembly election.He accused certain revenue and registration officials of facilitating patta transfers and registrations without proper documentation.Based on the petition and supporting documents, the district crime branch registered the case.Police said further investigation is under way to verify the allegations and establish whether fraudulent land transactions had taken place.
Article Summary: Kadayanallur DMK MLA T M Rajendran, his brother Chelladurai, VAO Arulmari, zonal deputy tahsildar Mohideen Pattani, land survey firka officer of Kurukkalpatti Usha and the sub-registrar of Melaneelithanallur.

Article Title: Loadman sustains 70% burns in fireworks unit chemical blast
Article Text:
file picture

Virudhunagar

:





A loadman suffered 70% burn injuries after an aluminium powder tin being unloaded from a truck slipped and exploded at a fireworks unit in Virudhunagar district on Tuesday evening.According to police sources, the incident occurred around 4.30pm at Karthika Fireworks unit owned by Murugan in Gangarsevalpatti near Alangulam.Workers were engaged in manufacturing firecrackers required for the Diwali festival across more than 50 rooms.Police said aluminium powder tins were being unloaded from a truck when one of the tins accidentally slipped and exploded. The blast subsequently triggered an explosion in a nearby chemical godown, and one of the godowns was flattened. The truck was completely gutted by the fire.A loadman identified as Pulithurai, 25, of Sivakasi sustained more than 70% burn injuries. He was rushed to the Sivakasi govt hospital for treatment.A team from Vembakottai fire station was engaged in firefighting operations.Vembakottai police have registered a case.
Article Summary: Aluminium powder tins were being unloaded from a truck when one of the tins accidentally slipped and exploded. The blast subsequently triggered an explosion in a nearby chemical godown. A loadman identified as Pulithurai, 25, of Sivakasi sustained more than 70% burn injuries.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: CMRL case: ED registers ECIRs against Pinarayi, Riyas
Article Text:
Pinarayi Vijayan & PA Mohamed Riyas

Kochi/Thiruvananthapuram:





The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has reportedly registered two Enforcement Case Information Reports (ECIRs) against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas in the CMRL-Exalogic monthly pay-off and hawala cases.The move follows the registration of two Vigilance cases, in which Vijayan and Riyas are the first accused. The ED will investigate the two cases separately.The Kerala High Court will deliver its verdict on Thursday on whether to allow Vijayan to appeal against the order directing the Vigilance department to register an FIR and investigate the monthly pay-off allegations.Meanwhile, the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) has formed two special investigation teams to probe the cases based on information provided by the ED.SP E N Suresh will head the team probing alleged payments by Cochin Minerals and Rutile Ltd (CMRL) to Veena’s company, Exalogic Solutions, during the first Pinarayi govt. The ED had alleged that the payments amounted to illegal gratification intended for Vijayan. Veena is the second accused, while CMRL MD S Sasidharan Kartha is also among the accused.SP Balakrishnan will lead the team probing allegations that Riyas accumulated illicit funds and transferred them abroad through hawala channels. Riyas is the first accused and Veena the second accused in this case. His associates are among the other accused.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has reportedly registered two Enforcement Case Information Reports (ECIRs) against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and former minister P A Mohamed Riyas. The Kerala High Court will deliver its verdict on Thursday on whether to allow Vijayan to appeal against the order directing the Vigilance department to register an FIR.

Article Title: Plaint against DGP Sreejith: Kerala HC slams govt for selective nod for inquiries
Article Text:
Kochi:





The high court has orally criticised the state govt for selectively granting permission to conduct inquiries against certain persons while withholding it in other cases.Justice A Badharudeen made the remarks while considering a petition filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Kannur, seeking a vigilance inquiry into allegations against DGP S Sreejith. The court observed that it should not have to intervene to ensure that investigations are conducted. If investigations could be initiated only at the court’s direction, what was the need for a govt, the court orally remarked, adding that the state govt must discharge its responsibilities.According to the petitioner, Sreejith, while serving as transport commissioner, had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad while wearing his police uniform. The petitioner also raised allegations concerning the printing contract for driving licences and RC books during Sreejith’s tenure as commissioner.While considering the petition, the court asked why so many allegations had been raised against a particular officer when other officers who had previously held the same post had left office with a good track record. The bench further adjourned the petition to Oct 26, allowing the state govt and Sreejith to file their replies to the allegations raised in the petition.
Article Summary: The high court has orally criticised the state govt for selectively granting permission to conduct inquiries against certain persons while withholding it in other cases. Justice A Badharudeen made the remarks while considering a petition filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Kannur, seeking a vigilance inquiry into allegations against DGP S Sreejith.

Article Title: Add photos, videos of illegal vehicle modifications in accident reports, Kerala HC tells transport commissioner
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has directed the transport commissioner to ensure that colour photographs and videos showing unauthorised modifications to vehicles involved in accidents are uploaded to the e-DAR portal as part of the accident reports.A bench of Justices Anil K Narendran and S Muralee Krishna issued the order in a suo motu petition initiated by the HC concerning unauthorised vehicle modifications. The court directed that reports uploaded by inspecting officers must include details of any violations of safety standards that increase the risk or severity of bodily injury to a person hit by the vehicle’s bodywork or brushing against it in the event of a collision, attracting punishment under the Motor Vehicles Act . The vehicle modification details uploaded to the e-DAR portal must also include any unauthorised alterations intended to increase engine horsepower and performance, as well as modifications to the braking system provided by the manufacturer.The transport commissioner, however, pointed out a technical issue with printed copies of the accident reports, in which photographs uploaded to the e-DAR portal did not appear. Accordingly, the court suo motu impleaded the National Informatics Centre (NIC) to address the issue and directed the state police chief to ensure compliance with its earlier directions on road safety and vehicle modifications. The court adjourned the matter to Oct 28.
Article Summary: The high court has directed the transport commissioner to ensure that colour photographs and videos showing unauthorised modifications to vehicles involved in accidents are uploaded to the e-DAR portal. A bench of Justices Anil K Narendran and S Muralee Krishna issued the order in a suo motu petition.

Article Title: Child rights panel probes youth’s suicide linked to police action
Article Text:
Thrissur

:

TOI





Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a suo motu case in connection with the suicide of a youth from Eriyad, near Kodungallur, in the district.The move follows serious allegations by the deceased’s father, Naushad Pazhupparambil, an Eriyad native, against Kodungallur Police over the circumstances leading to his son Aslam’s death.Naushad alleged that Aslam was taken into custody after being falsely implicated in a case linked to a relationship with a girl from Kodungallur. He said police subjected his son to severe physical and mental harassment, contributing to the suicide.Aslam was a minor when the alleged offence took place but was an adult when police initiated action against him, police said.“We have sought reports from the district police chief and district child protection officer on the allegations. If the reports establish that the deceased had attained the age of majority, we will take appropriate legal action,” said commission member Jalajamol T C, in response to queries fromThe case was registered allegedly based on the girl’s family’s complaint, Naushad said. He alleged that Aslam’s elder brother, Sahal, was also summoned to the police station. When Sahal witnessed the police assaulting Aslam, he confessed to the alleged offence in an attempt to spare his younger brother from further torture, Naushad said. Police subsequently named Sahal too as an accused in the case. Sahal is now in judicial custody, said his father.Police, however, maintain that the case was registered based on evidence, including digital evidence, indicating that the young woman was allegedly blackmailed and money was extorted from her.The two brothers allegedly extorted Rs 50,000 and 20 sovereigns of gold from the girl in Oct 2025, police said. The accused purchased an Innova car after selling the gold allegedly obtained from her, police added.The girl’s family has accused the brothers of blackmailing her and extorting money and gold. In a social media post, the girl’s sister said the family possessed sufficient evidence to substantiate the complaint and would produce it before the court. She said she was prepared to go to any lengths to secure justice.
Article Summary: Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a suo motu case in connection with the suicide of a youth. The move follows serious allegations by the deceased’s father, Naushad Pazhupparambil, an Eriyad native, against Kodungallur Police over the circumstances leading to his son Aslam's death.
